record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of greedy triangulations can be improved beyond π/6.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Is the α-value for greedy triangulations greater than π/6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Given a finite point set $P$ in the Euclidean plane, the greedy triangulation of $P$ is constructed as follows: order all $\binom{|P|}{2}$ straight-line segments between pairs of points in non-decreasing order of length, and process them in this order, adding a segment to the current edge set whenever it does not properly cross any previously added segment. The resulting plane graph $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ is a triangulation of the convex hull of $P$.

For a real number $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$, an edge $e=uv$ of a plane graph is said to satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property if at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as base and base angles equal to $\alpha$ contains no vertex of the graph (other than $u$ and $v$) in its interior. A plane graph has the $\alpha$-diamond property if every edge does. Whenever a plane triangulation has the $\alpha$-diamond property, it is a $t$-spanner of the complete Euclidean graph on its vertex set, with stretch factor $t$ bounded by an explicit function of $\alpha$ that decreases as $\alpha$ increases.

It is known that, for every finite point set $P$, the greedy triangulation $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property for $\alpha=\pi/6$.

Question. Let $\alpha^{*}$ denote the supremum of all $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ such that for every finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ the greedy triangulation $\mathrm{GT}(P)$ satisfies the $\alpha$-diamond property. Determine whether $\alpha^{*}>\pi/6$, and if so, give the best possible value of $\alpha^{*}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results discuss the α-diamond property, the greedy triangulation, and known stretch bounds for α-diamond triangulations, but no source was found that improves the guaranteed α-value for greedy triangulations beyond π/6 or proves π/6 to be tight. The status appears unresolved in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.snippet: Greedy triangulation fulfils the α-diamond-property; stretch bound depends on α.
status_evidence.claim: Greedy triangulations satisfy the α-diamond property and the resulting stretch bound depends monotonically on α.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on path-greedy spanners; does not report a resolution of the greedy-triangulation α-diamond constant.
